title: Early prediction of a relevant coronary arterial disease by patients with malignancies
summary:
Cardio-oncology is an important interface between oncology and cardiology, involving a continuously growing patient population cared for by both disciplines. The treatment of cancer patients with novel and/or established cancer therapies leads to longer life expectancy and the potential development of age-related or therapy-related cardiovascular diseases.

Several studies have shown that cancer patients have an increased risk of myocardial infarction. Common risk scores for coronary artery disease appear not to be effectively applicable in cancer patients. A variety of cancer therapies may worsen previously unrecognized coronary artery calcification or promote a tendency toward blood clot formation, including in the coronary arteries.

According to our hypothesis, by identifying individual risk factors, we can predict the need for invasive coronary intervention during the early stages of cancer therapy. We hope that this will help reduce the proportion of unplanned coronary interventions that are unfavorable from the perspective of cancer therapy and cancer prognosis.

For this purpose, we will use previously collected data from the Data Integration Center of the University Medical Center Freiburg. Based on the available data, such as blood tests, imaging procedures, etc., we plan to identify new risk factors that may predict clinically relevant coronary artery disease.
